title: CCTV Network Maintenance, Repair & Installation
description: The Council is looking to award a Contract for the provision of a suitably qualified and experienced Contractor to maintain the existing network and install new systems and equipment throughout the areas of the CCTV hubs responsibility. The CCTV Hub is located in a dedicated Council building in Blackburn. The CCTV Hub amalgamates the CCTV feeds for 6 local authority areas - Blackburn with Darwen, Burnley, Hyndburn, Pendle, Preston and Rossendale - in to a single CCTV monitoring hub. The Council wants to work with a Contractor that understands our values, positively supports the Council's objectives and will deliver an effective high quality CCTV Network Maintenance Service.

title: Provision of Bikeability Training in Lancashire Lot 2: Burnley, Lot 12: Lancaster
description:
"Bikeability is the Department for Transport's (DfT) flagship national cycling training programme for school children in England. It is a practical cycle training programme which provides school children with a life skill and enables them to cycle confidently and competently. Bikeability funding is distributed annually to local highway authorities, which the Authority is classified as. 

An open procurement procedure was conducted by the Authority in early 2024 to establish a multi-lotted, multi-provider framework to deliver Bikeability training on behalf of the Authority for the periods 2024/2025, 2025/2026, 2026/2027 and 2027/2028. The Framework was divided into 12 Lots based on the districts of Lancashire: Lot 1: West Lancashire, Lot 2: Burnley, Lot 3: Chorley, Lot 4: Fylde, Lot 5: Hyndburn, Lot 6: Pendle, Lot 7: Preston, Lot 8: Ribble Valley, Lot 9: Rossendale, Lot 10: South Ribble, Lot 11: Wyre, Lot 12: Lancaster. During the procurement process, no tender responses were received for Lot 2: Burnley and Lot 12: Lancaster. 

The aim of this procurement is to establish service provision for Lot 2: Burnley and Lot 12: Lancaster. The framework will have an initial term of 12 months running from 1st April 2025 to 31st March 2026. There will be the option to extend beyond the initial term to a maximum of a further 24 months in tranches of 12 months. "

title: Harehill Extra Care Housing
description:
Harehill is a purpose built extra care scheme owned by RBH (landlord). The scheme has 43 units of accommodation and the Council have nomination rights to 35 of 43 units of accommodation and 8 units remain the responsibility of RBH.\r
\r
Extra Care Housing provides care, support and well-being provision which is available over a 24 hour period, 7 days a week to individuals that have been assessed as being eligible under the Care Act 2014 for care and support.\r
\r
Extra Care provides choice for people that have changing care and support needs, allowing people to retain independence for longer with 24 hour flexible care and support and help in an emergency while living in a self-contained flat.\r
\r
The contract value, based on c. 320 planned hours per week is in the region of £330,000 per annum which will vary in response to the changing needs of residents.\r
\r
The contract will be re-tendered for 3 years and an option to extend further 2 years subject to satisfactory outcomes.\r
\r
Care, Support and Well-being provision will be available over a 24-hour period, 7 days a week\r

title: The Provision of Domiciliary Care Services:  Older People & Adult Physical Disabilities;  Older People & Adult Physical Disabilities - Rural
description:
Provision of Blackburn with Darwen General Domiciliary Care Services:  Older People & Adult Physical Disabilities; Older People & Adult Physical Disabilities - Rural
Providers will be responsible for providing personal, domestic, social, emotional and
rehabilitative care where appropriate, to enable service users to continue to live in their own
homes and maintain as far as possible their independence and usual / preferred lifestyle.
Providers are required to give assistance to people in their own homes which will meet their
assessed care needs and will often include elements of personal care and other tasks as
defined in the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2010, and
as set out by the Care Quality Commission. The tasks and outcomes to be delivered will be
described for each service user on the support plan, which will be completed at the time of
the first commissioning of service.
